Hi Samir —

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. Per our call I attached a one-page MAP (MAP-Orion-Pilot-Q4.xlsx) with the proposed milestones for the evaluation pilot, legal/ procurement gating, and production onramp. High level: 6-week technical evaluation (pilot), then a 2–3 week contract close window to get MSA + Order Form in place, with the DPA either signed in parallel or accepted via our standard addendum path.

Key asks from your side for sequencing:
- Confirm who is the primary signatory for the MSA and whether procurement will require an executed DPA before pilot data access.
- Any mandatory evidence packets (SOC 2, encryption configs, retained logs) we should push earlier in the MAP.
- Desired start date for pilot (we penciled in Oct 12).

If procurement needs the DPA first, we can propose a gated pilot that restricts data egress until DPA execution; otherwise, we can start with a synthetic/anon dataset earlier.

I've also flagged an optional fallback path in tab “Fallbacks” that allows a 30-day pilot with a scoped Order Form while legal finalizes the DPA. Please review and tell us what procurement needs so we can lock the target signature windows.

Attachments: MAP-Orion-Pilot-Q4.xlsx (MAP draft), SOC2-summary.pdf (summary of our controls).

Thanks —
Dylan Brooks

Dylan — thanks for the MAP. Couple of items from procurement/legal that will determine sequencing:

1) Our legal team requires an executed DPA before any production data is shared. We can accept a limited pilot on de-identified data with PII blocked, but anything with live PHI requires DPA in place.
2) For the MSA: procurement prefers the MSA executed before the order form if there are custom SLA or indemnity changes — otherwise we can sign the order form first for pilot spend and roll to a master order later.
3) Evidence: SOC 2 attestation and the data retention policy (we saw your SOC2-summary, but will need the full assertion or ISO control mapping).
4) Timeline: legal has a 10 business day review window once they receive redlines. Can you do a 10-business-day turnaround if we mark the MAP as “target signature start” on Oct 6?

If you can provide a clean DPA (or a redline window doc) and the full assertion this week, we can try to align legal to start review next Monday. Also cc’ing procurement for the PO timing.

—Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Security & Compliance, Orion Health AI

Samir — appreciate the clarity. Quick sequencing proposal from our side to keep the pilot moving while satisfying legal constraints: 

1) Week 0 (Oct 5): Turnover package — full SOC2 assertion, encryption diagram, retention policy, and our standard DPA template with a short summary of any deviations. (Attachment: redlines_MSA_v1.docx for reference — contains our suggested minimal edits to speed review.)
2) Week 1–2 (Oct 12–23): Legal review window (10 business days). During this period we propose starting a synthetic-data pilot or a de-identified dataset runbook that Orion can use to validate integration. No production PHI access until DPA executes.
3) Week 3 (Oct 26–30): Target signature week — MSA executed, Order Form countersigned for pilot licensing. DPA either executed or executed with an interim technical controls attestation and a commitment to finalize within 10 business days post-MSA.

Fallbacks if DPA is delayed beyond 20 business days:
- Option A: Scoped staging environment with restricted data egress and audit hooks enabled; production access gated to a named SRE/engineering account.
- Option B: Extended evaluation on synthetic data and a 20% pilot fee credit if production onboarding is delayed more than 30 calendar days from target signature.

We can provide a DocuSign envelope for the MSA + Order Form and a separate link for the DPA to keep workflows independent. That should allow procurement to PO against the order form while legal finalizes DPA text.

If that sequencing works, Dylan — can you confirm internal approval for the credit fallback and the gated-access technical plan? If so, I'll prepare the two DocuSign envelopes and the turn-key evidence package.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Sales Operations & Contracts, Redwood Inference
